subject.title: Telegram: specific forum topic becomes permanent inbound black hole after stuck-session recovery

question: For Telegram stuck-session recovery, should later same-lane updates drain only after a hard cancellation or process-restart boundary, and should recovery also clear persisted per-topic routing or dedupe state for the affected forum topic?
rationale: The current code proves a guarded-lane failure family, but the reported post-restart forum-topic black hole needs a safety decision before a narrow automated patch can avoid either concurrent same-lane execution or an incomplete persistent-state fix.

options.title: Require Hard Boundary First
options.body: Keep this issue open until the Telegram recovery design kills or isolates the old handler before later same-lane updates drain, then add live or crash-window proof for forum topics.

options.title: Treat Persistent State Separately
options.body: Land a narrow in-process guarded-lane fix only if it clearly leaves this issue open for persisted topic routing or dedupe investigation.

options.title: Accept Guarded Serialization
options.body: If maintainers prefer never releasing a lane while old work may still run, document that tradeoff and track a user-visible recovery command instead.

recommendation.title: Require Hard Boundary First
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open until the Telegram recovery design kills or isolates the old handler before later same-lane updates drain, then add live or crash-window proof for forum topics.

likelyOwner.reason: The latest maintainer review on the related PR states the concrete safety boundary that must be decided before this failure family can be fixed.
